title: Measles confirmed in 45 states in 2026: CDC data shows kids and teens hit hardest - masslive.com
snippet:
In 2026, 7% of people with the virus — 151 people — were hospitalized.

That’s down from 11% last year. The drop was steepest among kids under 5, whose hospitalization rate nearly halved from 18% to 10%.

As of July 2026, there have been zero measles deaths in the U.S. versus three in 2025.

## Why is this happening?

CDC data points to a drop in vaccination rates alongside the hike in measles cases. [...] The surge isn’t random — it stems from a series of outbreaks.

The CDC has tracked 35 new outbreaks this year. An outbreak is considered a cluster of three or more cases in a given community.

In 2026, a staggering 93% of all cases trace back to a single outbreak.

Patients who were unvaccinated accounted for 93% of the cases — matching last year’s trend.

## The one bright spot

Fewer patients infected with measles are ending up hospitalized this year compared with previous years. [...] Kindergarten MMR coverage has dropped from 95.2% in the 2019-2020 school year to 92.5% today — below the 95% level needed for herd immunity.

That gap adds up to roughly 286,000 kindergartners without full protection last school year.

## Measles state-by-state data

CDC has real-time dashboards running in Arizona, Pennsylvania, Utah and Virginia, plus parent-friendly guidance on spotting symptoms early.
